<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bf69cb41cc1f6351b0b0365ad7842a561611190f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4c17477143143457fc61a885d50e69422b4dd3e3` — the merge of head `eb4c293266785438310dfe89120f442a9a6d2919` into base `bf69cb41cc1f6351b0b0365ad7842a561611190f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4c17477143143457fc61a885d50e69422b4dd3e3 && git checkout 4c17477143143457fc61a885d50e69422b4dd3e3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bf69cb41cc1f6351b0b0365ad7842a561611190f eb4c293266785438310dfe89120f442a9a6d2919 && git checkout -B drift-repro bf69cb41cc1f6351b0b0365ad7842a561611190f && git merge --no-ff eb4c293266785438310dfe89120f442a9a6d2919

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bf69cb41cc1f6351b0b0365ad7842a561611190f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bf69cb41cc1f6351b0b0365ad7842a561611190f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b64d1bdfc31257073a6f4011075e2604970750da`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.record-currency-sibling-extension-judged-as-served.ts + packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-batch-object-registration.test.ts

Inputs read: card #33911 (body, triage first touch, claim, os-dev-report), PR #35538 (body, the four-file list, the net diff against merge-base 895dd437), and the check-runs on the head. The changeset is prose and is not reviewed; it is quoted once below only because it carries a sentence the reviewed files have to agree with.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set, `object_extension` published single save (`PUT /api/v1/meta/object_extension/NAME`, faces `meta-envelope` and `meta-dispatch`): a record-mode `currency` field whose one-segment `currencyField` names no other field of the object as served, the amount itself, or a field that is not a code field, moves from 200 to 422 `INVALID_METADATA`. Right: it is the card's expected answer, and the door is reached through the existing `objectRegistrationRefusal(..., 'extend', { againstRegistry: true })` call in `protocol-save.ts`, which this diff does not touch.
- Accept-set, batch writers (package duplicate, unmanaged import, package publish, stored-metadata migration pass) and the end of an install, upgrade or reload run: the same pair is now refused there too, because the new loop sits inside `followRefusalsOf`, which every asker of the follow door shares. Right, and the entry's `surface` names all three.
- Accept-set, owner layers: the loop runs for every layer, so an owner single save or owner run is refused when the served object holds a dangling sibling pointer an extension adds. Right in design (it is ruling R3 and R6 applied to the sibling form, as pair (a) already behaves on `main`), but only half of it is declared; see S1.
- Accept-set, pointers of three or more segments on an extension: `recordCurrencyPathOf` answers `undefined` for them, so the new loop judges them as a sibling name and refuses. Right: no row can hold such a key.
- Not changed: the cold boot and stored-row hydration (never asked), `ObjectSchema` and `ObjectExtensionSchema` (`object.zod.ts` untouched), draft saves (body-only question), and the per-item publish of an `object_extension` draft, which asks the registry only for type `object`. The entry claims none of these. Right as a description; the last one is escalated in ③.
- Public surface: no new export. `recordCurrencySiblingCodeError` and `siblingCodeFieldCandidates` are module-private; `followPairKey` gains a private kind. `RecordCurrencyFollowRefusedError` keeps its code, status and fields. The spec registry gains one semantic entry. Right.
- Gate verdicts on the head: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), every Lint family, Test Core 1 to 10, Test UI 1 to 16, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, PR-body guards and Check PR Size all concluded success. Skipped runs are opt-in or not triggered by this file list. No failure, none pending.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql` minor, declared BREAKING accept-set narrowing, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both the PR body and the changeset, and the ADR-0087 disposition `registered record-currency-sibling-extension-judged-as-served` matching the entry id. This matches what the diff publishes: a refusal where a save was accepted, no new export, no schema key. The entry file lives in `@objectstack/spec`, which is not named in the changeset; `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/objectql` are in the same `fixed` group in `.changeset/config.json`, so the entry ships in the same release. Check Changeset concluded success. Clause-②: no (narrowing) holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation, entry file outside the claim's declared surface: accepted. A `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` changeset owes a registered semantic entry, the file adds no schema key and no export, and it is exactly what makes this PR a schema-face review.
- Deviation, `protocol-save.ts` not edited: confirmed in the tree. Its `object_extension` branch already asks the door against the served fold.
- Deviation, PR footer and commit trailer form: lane-seat matter, no effect on the contract.
- Deviation, three build-prerequisite gate rows re-run after the closure build: superseded by the head's check-runs, all success.
- `open_questions`: none raised.
- Out-of-scope finding, noted and not filed by the dev: a two-segment pointer on an extension whose first segment is not a `master_detail` of the served object. Confirmed by reading: `recordCurrencyPathOf` returns a path with `master` undefined, pair (a) skips it and the new pair (b) skips every two-segment pointer, so no served-object door judges it. It is the same class as this card (saved, then no write of the amount can succeed) and outside this card's one-segment title. Escalated: the seat files it as its own card rather than leaving it in PR notes.
- Escalated with it, read off the tree and not measured: `promoteDraftForPublish` asks the registry's follow door only for type `object`, so an `object_extension` saved as a draft and then published per item appears to reach the registry without the follow door being asked, for pair (a) and the new pair (b) alike. It predates this diff and the entry does not claim that door, so it is not a finding here; it needs a measurement at the public door and a card.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff reads in-memory field maps of the registry only; no query, no id materialisation, no in-app join.
- Security: nothing security-shaped found.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing itself, against the published spec on `main`. `ObjectSchema` (`refuseDishonestRecordCurrencyField`) already refuses a record-mode amount whose sibling pointer names no other declared field, the amount itself, a field of a non-code type, or a `text` field without `valueDomain: 'iso_4217_currency'`. Its docblock carves `ObjectExtensionSchema` out for one stated reason: the pointer may name a field only the owner declares. That carve-out never declared a pointer into nothing as a capability, and the write path (`record-currency-code.ts`) refuses every write of such an amount. So the narrowing takes no declared capability away at the consumer; it makes the spec's own refusal real at the first door that holds the served field map. Every shape the carve-out exists for stays admitted: a code field of the owner, of the same extension body, or of another enabled extension.

`record-currency-aggregate-door.ts`, sentence by sentence against the code:
- "names no other field of the object as served, or a field that holds no ISO 4217 code": holds. `pointer !== field` plus an own-property test on the served map, then `isRecordCurrencyCodeField`, the spec's own predicate, so the code-field test cannot drift from the spec.
- "Judged at the registration of any of the object's layers": holds; the loop is unconditional on ownership.
- The R6 wording: holds. `extensionPackageOf` withholds disabled packages, as the served fold does.
- The pair key `sibling / object / field / pointer` is stable across the two readings the `before` comparison makes, so a run that only adds a code field elsewhere does not turn an old pair into a new one.
- Attempts to break it: a self-pointer (refused), a pointer at an inherited prototype key (own-property test), a `null` field value (refused as no field), a pre-existing bad pair listed ahead of a new good field (the generator keeps going past pairs already in `before`), an extension from a disabled package supplying the code field (not counted, as R5 rules for pair (a)). None broke the door.

Findings:

- S1 (should-fix) — the entry understates what a single save does with a pointer that was already dangling. Its `reason` says "A run that leaves such a pointer as it found it is not refused over it". That is true of a registration run only. A single save and the batch writers ask with the slot left empty (`judgeRegistrationDoors` passes `before: null`), so: re-publishing an unchanged extension that already carries the bad pointer is refused, and so is any published single save of an own-layer owner while an extension's amount dangles, whether or not the owner changed anything. The sibling entry `record-currency-follow-extension-judged-as-served` states exactly this for pair (a) ("A single save and the batch writers judge against the slot left empty, so re-publishing an unchanged extension ... is refused there") and gives the owner its prescription; this entry drops both, and its `replacement` covers the owner only when it "drops or de-codes" the field. It matters more here than for pair (a): the card's own bug stored these rows with a 200 on 18.5.0, so they exist on running servers, not only in packages a cold boot admitted. The changeset's line "A re-save that leaves such a pointer as it found it is not refused over it" is the same statement in its false form. Fix: add the single-save and batch sentence and the unchanged-owner prescription to the entry, and bring the changeset line into agreement.
- S2 (should-fix) — the test that says it pins this pins nothing. In the last case of the new describe, the assertion commented "A no-change re-save of the owner is not refused over a pair it leaves as it found it" re-saves an owner that declares `currency_code`, with the extension pointing at it: no refused pair exists in that state, so it would pass with the `before` comparison deleted. Neither behaviour of the sibling pair is pinned: not the run-level R7 (pair (a) has `manifest.register` cases for it on `main`), and not the single-save refusal over a pre-existing dangling pointer that S1 describes. Fix: pin both, or at least correct the comment and add the single-save case.
- N1 (nit) — the docblock calls `recordCurrencySiblingCodeError` "the served-object twin of `ObjectSchema`'s sibling-pointer refusal", but the loop reads `recordCurrencyFieldOf`, which answers only for `type: 'currency'`. The spec's refusal also judges a `summary` declaring `currencyMode: 'record'` and a `formula` returning currency. Those are not written, so the card's failure (every write refused) does not arise, and the entry's "record-mode amount" stays accurate for what a consumer can hit; the word "twin" is wider than the code. A follow-up card can decide whether an extension's record-mode summary pointer should be judged as served.
- N2 (nit) — `siblingCodeFieldCandidates` is a second copy of the private `codeFieldCandidates` in the spec's `record-currency-path.ts`, and the sibling sentence lives in objectql while the messages of pairs (a), (c) and (d) live in that spec module "so the two judgements cannot drift". No effect on behaviour today.
